subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Foundations: What Holds a Bridge Up from Below
description: A quick, practical guide to Foundations: What Holds a Bridge Up from Below.

hook.text: The Brooklyn Bridge's foundations go 24 meters below the riverbed. Workers dug in pressurized air chambers.

buildup.text: Caissons are watertight boxes sunk to the riverbed. Workers inside excavated mud while air pressure held water out.

discovery.text: Decompression sickness — 'the bends' — crippled workers who surfaced too fast. The cause was unknown in 1870.

twist.text: Chief engineer Washington Roebling got the bends so badly he directed construction from his bedroom with binoculars.

climax.text: Modern foundations use drilled shafts sunk 100 meters into bedrock. No human enters the hole.

punchline.text: Every great bridge starts with a hole in the ground.

quiz.question: What medical condition affected Brooklyn Bridge workers in the caissons?
options: Decompression sickness from surfacing too fast
Lead poisoning from the construction materials
